title: Circle theorems
lede: Arcs, chords, tangents and the surprising rules that connect their angles. Plus arc length and sector area, the math of tire wear and pizza slices.

sections.md:
## Parts of a circle
| Part | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **radius** | center to the edge |
| **diameter** | edge to edge through the center (2 radii) |
| **chord** | any segment with both ends on the circle (the diameter is the longest) |
| **secant** | a line that cuts through the circle at two points |
| **tangent** | a line that **touches** the circle at exactly one point |
| **arc** | a piece of the circle's edge |
| **sector** | a pizza-slice region between two radii |

## Central and inscribed angles
A **central angle** has its vertex at the **center**. Its measure **equals** the arc it cuts off: a 80° central angle cuts an 80° arc.

An **inscribed angle** has its vertex **on the circle**. Its measure is **half** the arc it cuts off.

**Inscribed angle = ½ × intercepted arc**

sections.md:
## Three consequences
1. **Inscribed angles on the same arc are equal.** Every point P on the far side sees AB at the same angle.
2. **An angle inscribed in a semicircle is 90°.** The arc is 180°, half of that is 90°. (Thales' theorem: any triangle drawn with the diameter as one side and its third corner on the circle is a right triangle.)
3. **Opposite angles of a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle add to 180°.** Together they intercept the whole 360° circle, and half of 360° is 180°.

sections.md:
## Tangent facts
- A tangent is **perpendicular to the radius** at the point where it touches.
- Two tangents drawn from the same outside point are **equal in length**.

The first one makes many problems into right triangles, and then the Pythagorean theorem finishes them.

*A tangent from point P touches a circle of radius 5. P is 13 from the center. How long is the tangent segment?* The radius meets the tangent at 90°: 5² + t² = 13² → t = **12**.

## Arc length and sector area
An arc or sector is a **fraction** of the whole circle: **θ ÷ 360**.

- **Arc length** = (θ ÷ 360) × 2πr
- **Sector area** = (θ ÷ 360) × πr²

A 90° arc on a circle of radius 10: (90 ÷ 360) × 2π(10) = ¼ × 62.83 ≈ **15.7**.

sections.title: Tire math
sections.problem: A truck tire has a diameter of about 40 inches. How far does the truck move in one full rotation, and how many rotations per mile?
sections.answer: **≈126 inches per turn, about 504 turns per mile.** If worn tires shrink the diameter, the wheel turns more times per mile, and the speedometer, which counts rotations, reads a little **high**.

sections.label: Common traps
sections.md:
- **Inscribed vs central.** Center vertex = equal to the arc. Edge vertex = half the arc.
- **Arc measure vs arc length.** Measure is in **degrees**; length is a **distance**. Two arcs can both be 60° and have very different lengths on different-size circles.
- **Diameter vs radius** in formulas. Circumference = πd = 2πr. Area uses r.
- **The tangent-radius right angle** is often unmarked. You're expected to know it.

practice.why: Tangents from the same point are equal.

practice.q: Tangent from P touches a circle of radius 8. P is 17 from the center. Tangent length?
practice.why: Right angle at the tangent point: 8² + t² = 17² → t² = 289 − 64 = 225 → **t = 15**.

practice.q: Sector with a 45° angle in a circle of radius 12. Area, to 1 decimal? (π ≈ 3.1416)
Two inscribed angles intercept the same arc. One is 3x + 10, the other 5x − 20. Find x.
practice.why: Inscribed angles on the same arc are equal: 3x + 10 = 5x − 20 → 30 = 2x → **x = 15** (each angle is 55°).
